history.value: Wikipedia says the present depot was built on 23 February 1888 by the Chicago, Burlington and Quincy Railroad, replacing a Union Depot of 1853 that burned in 1885. The 1888 building originally included a hotel, restaurants, waiting rooms and rooms for railroad employees. In 1942 much of the station was torn down, leaving little more than the waiting room and ticket office. The building is now owned and preserved by the Mendota Museum and Historical Society as the Union Depot Railroad Museum, which the official Amtrak page also mentions, including a working HO model of central Mendota in the 1930s.

history.value: The official Amtrak page and Wikipedia agree that Los Angeles Union Station opened in May 1939.
